Residents of the Maple Street neighborhood are checking in on each other more often after a break-in at Daniel Kim's home last month left the longtime resident shaken but unharmed.
Kim was home at the time and briefly confronted the intruder before the person fled through a back door.
Kim has installed new locks and a doorbell camera since the incident.

Daniel Kim was recognized this week for completing three years as a weekly volunteer at the Westside Public Library, where he helps run the children's reading hour every Wednesday afternoon.
Branch manager Louis Ferreira said Kim has a gift for keeping young children engaged during story time and often brings in props or simple crafts tied to that week's book.
'Parents specifically ask if Daniel is reading before they decide which day to come in,' Ferreira said.
Kim said he started volunteering as a way to give back after moving to the neighborhood and has enjoyed watching some of the same kids grow up over the past three years.
The library plans to recognize Kim's contribution with a small certificate at its spring volunteer appreciation event.
